title: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation · Paper 2 (HL) — original full-format practice
subject: mathematics-applications-interpretation
instructions: An approved graphing calculator is required. Answer every question in its linked digital working area, preserving intermediate steps, units and graphs. No separate answer sheet is used.

resources.label: Original data set — energy demand
resources.text:
A campus recorded mean outdoor temperature T (°C) and daily electricity demand E (MWh):
T: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25
E: 31.2, 28.1, 25.4, 23.0, 21.9, 22.5, 25.1, 29.8

questions.label: Question 1 — nonlinear regression
questions.prompt: Use the energy-demand data to compare a linear model with a quadratic model. State suitable equations, compare their fit, and use the better model to estimate demand at 28°C. Comment on the reliability of the estimate.

questions.label: Question 2 — transition matrices
questions.prompt: A bike-share survey classifies users as occasional (O) or regular (R). Each month, 35% of O users become R and 15% of R users become O. Starting with 800 O users and 200 R users, construct a transition matrix, find the distribution after six months, and determine the long-term distribution.

questions.label: Question 3 — hypothesis testing
questions.prompt: A school claims that the median queue time in its cafeteria is 6 minutes. A random sample of 14 queue times is 4.1, 5.0, 5.2, 5.6, 5.8, 6.1, 6.3, 6.7, 7.0, 7.2, 7.8, 8.1, 9.0, 10.4. Perform a suitable test at the 5% level and state your conclusion in context.

questions.label: Question 4 — differential modelling
questions.prompt: The rate of change of an algae population P is modelled by dP/dt = 0.18P(1 − P/5000). Given P(0) = 400, use technology to estimate P(20), find when P first exceeds 4000, and explain the meaning of 5000 in the model.

questions.label: Question 5 — chi-squared test
questions.prompt: A survey records transport choice for 120 students by year group. Construct an appropriate contingency table from the supplied totals, perform a chi-squared test for independence at 5%, and state a contextual conclusion.

questions.label: Question 6 — graph theory
questions.prompt: A weighted graph models inspection routes between six sites. Use a nearest-neighbour upper bound and a deleted-vertex lower bound to propose a tour, then calculate the percentage gap between the bounds.

questions.label: Question 7 — differential equations
questions.prompt: A medicine concentration satisfies dC/dt = 12 − 0.25C with C(0)=0. Solve the equation, identify the limiting concentration, and find when the concentration first reaches 40 mg L⁻¹.

questions.label: Question 8 — optimization
questions.prompt: A manufacturer models unit cost by C(x) = 1800/x + 0.04x + 12 for 20 ≤ x ≤ 400. Find the output minimizing cost and perform a sensitivity check if the fixed-cost term changes by 10%.

questions.label: Question 9 — time series
questions.prompt: Quarterly sales show a linear trend with additive seasonal effects. Using the supplied eight-quarter pattern, calculate four-point moving averages, estimate seasonal components and forecast the next two quarters.

questions.label: Question 10 — inference
questions.prompt: Two independent samples compare battery life. Use technology to construct a 95% confidence interval for the difference in population means, test the manufacturer's claim, and state two assumptions.

questions.label: Question 11 — matrices
questions.prompt: A three-state migration model is represented by a stochastic matrix. Determine its stationary distribution, calculate the population after ten transitions, and explain one limitation of the Markov assumption.

questions.label: Question 12 — coupled modelling
questions.prompt: Build a piecewise model for a reservoir receiving seasonal inflow and constant demand. Use a spreadsheet or graphing technology to identify the first month storage falls below 20% and evaluate one demand-management proposal.
